messages.content: Predict one human response in a one-shot public-goods task. The task instructions describe six people, each endowed with USD 0.30 (30 cents). Each privately chooses either to contribute all 30 cents to a shared pot or to contribute nothing. They keep any money not contributed. A threshold condition, when present, specifies a minimum number of contributors needed for the public pot to succeed. If that threshold is not reached, ALL money in the pot is destroyed and each person receives only the money they kept. If the threshold is reached, the pot is doubled and split equally among all six people, including anyone who contributed nothing. In the baseline condition there is no threshold: the pot is always doubled and equally shared. Thus when it succeeds, a total of k contributors produces a return of 10k cents to each person, on top of their unspent endowment. Group decisions are matched after data collection; no realized choices by other members or final group outcome are provided at these response stages. Predict this person’s contribution now, before their later prediction of others’ contributions. Output only the integer contribution amount in US cents, either 0 or 30. No explanation.

Current task: choose whether to contribute the whole 30-cent endowment or keep it.
The threshold is 4 contributors out of six. Only you know for certain that you have seen this threshold instruction. You cannot be certain the others saw the same instruction; they cannot be certain you did. This does not mean they necessarily do not know the threshold. 
Stable personal descriptors (the exact survey position of these items is not documented): age 26 years; gender Female; highest education Bachelor’s Degree. No trust or socioeconomic scale scores are supplied.
No earlier contribution decision or feedback exists in this one-shot game. How many cents does this person contribute now?

Predict one human response in a one-shot public-goods task. The task instructions describe six people, each endowed with USD 0.30 (30 cents). Each privately chooses either to contribute all 30 cents to a shared pot or to contribute nothing. They keep any money not contributed. A threshold condition, when present, specifies a minimum number of contributors needed for the public pot to succeed. If that threshold is not reached, ALL money in the pot is destroyed and each person receives only the money they kept. If the threshold is reached, the pot is doubled and split equally among all six people, including anyone who contributed nothing. In the baseline condition there is no threshold: the pot is always doubled and equally shared. Thus when it succeeds, a total of k contributors produces a return of 10k cents to each person, on top of their unspent endowment. Group decisions are matched after data collection; no realized choices by other members or final group outcome are provided at these response stages. After making their contribution choice, the person is asked to predict how many of the OTHER FIVE group members will contribute. Their own already chosen contribution is known, but it does not count among these five. This Study 1 prediction does not carry the correct-prediction payment introduced in Study 2. Output only the predicted number of other contributors, one integer from 0 to 5. No explanation.

Output only the predicted number of other contributors, one integer from 0 to 5. No explanation.

Predict one human response in a one-shot public-goods task. The task instructions describe six people, each endowed with USD 0.30 (30 cents). Each privately chooses either to contribute all 30 cents to a shared pot or to contribute nothing. They keep any money not contributed. A threshold condition, when present, specifies a minimum number of contributors needed for the public pot to succeed. If that threshold is not reached, ALL money in the pot is destroyed and each person receives only the money they kept. If the threshold is reached, the pot is doubled and split equally among all six people, including anyone who contributed nothing. In the baseline condition there is no threshold: the pot is always doubled and equally shared. Thus when it succeeds, a total of k contributors produces a return of 10k cents to each person, on top of their unspent endowment. Group decisions are matched after data collection; no realized choices by other members or final group outcome are provided at these response stages. After making their contribution choice, the person is asked to predict how many of the OTHER FIVE group members will contribute. Their own already chosen contribution is known, but it does not count among these five. This Study 1 prediction does not carry the correct-prediction payment introduced in Study 2. Output only the predicted number of other contributors, one integer from 0 to 5. No explanation.

Predict one human response in a one-shot public-goods task. The task instructions describe six people, each endowed with USD 0.30 (30 cents). Each privately chooses either to contribute all 30 cents to a shared pot or to contribute nothing. They keep any money not contributed. If that threshold is not reached, ALL money in the pot is destroyed and each person receives only the money they kept. If the threshold is reached, the pot is doubled and split equally among all six people, including anyone who contributed nothing. Thus when it succeeds, a total of k contributors produces a return of 10k cents to each person, on top of their unspent endowment. Group decisions are matched after data collection; no realized choices by other members or final group outcome are provided at these response stages. Output only the predicted number of other contributors, one integer from 0 to 5. No explanation.

Output only the predicted number of other contributors, one integer from 0 to 5. No explanation.

Output only the predicted number of other contributors, one integer from 0 to 5. No explanation.

A threshold condition, when present, specifies a minimum number of contributors needed for the public pot to succeed. If that threshold is not reached, ALL money in the pot is destroyed and each person receives only the money they kept. If the threshold is reached, the pot is doubled and split equally among all six people, including anyone who contributed nothing. In the baseline condition there is no threshold: the pot is always doubled and equally shared. Thus when it succeeds, a total of k contributors produces a return of 10k cents to each person, on top of their unspent endowment. Group decisions are matched after data collection; no realized choices by other members or final group outcome are provided at these response stages. After making their contribution choice, the person is asked to predict how many of the OTHER FIVE group members will contribute. Their own already chosen contribution is known, but it does not count among these five. This Study 1 prediction does not carry the correct-prediction payment introduced in Study 2. Output only the predicted number of other contributors, one integer from 0 to 5. No explanation.

The threshold is 2 contributors out of six. Only you know for certain that you have seen this threshold instruction. You cannot be certain the others saw the same instruction; they cannot be certain you did. This does not mean they necessarily do not know the threshold.
